title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Extremely Light Foam (ELF)
description: ELF (Extremely Light Foam) is a new way to make structural foam that is both much lighter and much stronger than today�s alternatives. The process, developed by scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory, uses common epoxy materials mixed with tiny hollow particles and a temporary liquid that later evaporates. As the material cures, this liquid naturally leaves behind a well-organized network of empty space, creating a foam that is mostly air but still highly resistant to crushing and pressure. The result is a material that can be up to twice as strong at the same weight as conventional foams, while remaining easy to pour, mold, and manufacture at scale using safe, commercially available ingredients. Because it combines low weight, high strength, simple processing, and design flexibility, ELF is well suited for commercial applications in marine systems, aerospace and transportation, lightweight structural panels, insulation, and impact-absorbing components. How it Works: The technology works by intentionally using a temporary liquid during the curing of a polymer foam to shape its internal structure. When the liquid-filled mixture hardens, the liquid naturally separates from the solid material and later evaporates, leaving behind a network of tiny, well-distributed voids between microscopic hollow particles embedded in the polymer. By carefully controlling the type of liquid used and the curing conditions, these voids form in a predictable and repeatable way rather than randomly. This controlled internal architecture is what gives the material its unusual combination of low weight and high resistance to crushing, while still allowing the material to be poured, molded, and manufactured using standard industrial processes and readily available materials Key Advantages: Exceptionally low weight while maintaining high structural integrity, achieving densities well below conventional structural foams High resistance to crushing and compression, even under extreme pressures Simple, low-cost manufacturing process using standard equipment and commercially available materials Easy to cast and mold into complex shapes and large parts without specialized tooling Safe and non-hazardous materials, supporting easier handling and regulatory acceptance Multifunctional performance, offering structural support, thermal insulation, and impact energy absorption in a single material Market Applications: Marine & Offshore (lightweight buoyancy materials, pressure-tolerant structures) Aerospace (weight-saving structural cores, multifunctional insulation materials) Defense & Security (lightweight structural components, energy-absorbing materials) Transportation & Mobility (mass reduction materials, impact and vibration mitigation) Advanced Composites & Manufacturing (core materials for sandwich structures, moldable lightweight fillers) Energy & Industrial Systems (lightweight structural insulation, protective housings) Thermal & Acoustic Solutions (lightweight insulation panels, noise-damping materials) Development Status: TRL 3 US Patent pending LA-UR-26-21224 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: EMU Electric Modernization Upgrade
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) has developed and intends to field a modular, organic capability consisting of commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components integrated into custom hardware for the MH-60R Seahawk helicopter. The Government has established a viable system baseline, however, a standardized, repeatable, and supportable production, deployment, and sustainment process is not yet developed. With an initial operational capability target of Q1 FY2028, the program's small scope makes traditional, large-scale support and depot-level sustainment models highly cost-prohibitive. The current ad-hoc model lacks a process with defined material flow, supply-chain management, quality control, and software deployment process. Consequently, ongoing assembly and support practices require excessive time and specialized personnel that a small team cannot realistically maintain. Furthermore, the existing packaging is not optimized for rapid global air transport, and the chassis design needs human factors optimization for installation and removal in shipboard and austere environments. As a result, these cumulative limitations reduce overall operational availability, increase the burden on forward-deployed personnel, and raise long-term lifecycle costs. This delays the Navy's critical ability to rapidly produce, transport, install, and sustain this capability worldwide. Desired Outcomes & Constraints (Submissions may be for one or all requirements) 1. ?Process Design: Production Process: An operational, production-representative process capable of producing a defined pilot lot using controlled material, assembly, programming, inspection, test, configuration-management, packaging, and acceptance processes that is executable by a small team. Deployment Process: A lightweight, practical support process that enables a small team to provision and deploy the capability with minimal specialized infrastructure. Sustainment Process: A lightweight, practical support process that enables a small team to support, maintain, repair, reconfigure, and reconstitute the capability with minimal specialized infrastructure. 2. description: Für das Projekt Neubau ESTW Guben / Wellmitz werden umfangreiche Infrastrukturmaßnahmen im Bahnhof Guben durchgeführt. Das Vorhaben umfasst die Errichtung der bahnseitigen Leistungen für das neue ESTW Guben, die Erneuerung der Gleisfeldbeleuchtung sowie umfassende Oberbauarbeiten zur Anpassung der Gleisanlagen. Ziel der Maßnahme ist die Modernisierung der Betriebs- und Infrastrukturanlagen, um einen zukunftssicheren, leistungsfähigen und wirtschaftlichen Bahnbetrieb zu gewährleisten. Das Projekt gliedert sich in zwei Lose. Los 1 beinhaltet die Bahnmarkleistungen für das ESTW Guben einschließlich der erforderlichen Kabeltiefbau- und Tiefbaumaßnahmen, der Herstellung von Signalgründungen, Kabeltrassen, Kabelschächten und Kabelkanälen sowie der Gestaltung des ESTW-Standortes mit Zufahrten, Gehwegen, Stellflächen, Entwässerungsanlagen und Einfriedungen. Darüber hinaus werden bestehende Stellwerksanlagen und zugehörige Infrastruktur zurückgebaut bzw. angepasst. Ebenfalls Bestandteil von Los 1 ist die vollständige Erneuerung der Gleisfeldbeleuchtung im Bahnhof Guben. Hierzu werden neue Beleuchtungsverteilungen, Kabelanlagen, Beleuchtungsmasten, Erdungsanlagen und moderne LED-Beleuchtungssysteme errichtet sowie die bestehende Gleisfeldbeleuchtungsanlage zurückgebaut. Los 2 umfasst die Anpassung und Erneuerung der Gleisanlagen im Zusammenhang mit der ESTW-Inbetriebnahme. Dazu gehören die Erneuerung der Weichen 10 und 54, die Einkürzung und Erneuerung des Gleises 50 einschließlich der Herstellung eines neuen Gleisabschlusses sowie die erforderlichen Schotter-, Stopf-, Schweiß- und Vermessungsarbeiten. Die Oberbauarbeiten dienen der Anpassung der Gleisinfrastruktur an die künftigen betrieblichen Anforderungen des neuen Stellwerks und gewährleisten die langfristige Betriebssicherheit der Anlage. Nicht Bestandteil dieser Projektbeschreibung sind Leistungen der Telekommunikationstechnik . Sämtliche TK-Anlagen, Übertragungstechnik, GSM-R-, DB-MAS- sowie weitere Telekommunikationssysteme werden im Rahmen separater Vergaben bzw. durch andere Auftragnehmer realisiert.
